To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a synthetic HBsAg, pre-S(2), region synthetic peptide, p 120-145, is a T cell determinant and that it is capable of priming T cells that can provide help for B cell production of antibodies that bind to the native HBsAg, p33 particles.

a synthetic peptide containing a T cell recognition site on the pre-S(2), region of hepatitis B surface antigen is a highly immunogenic T cell epitope that is able to prime T cell help to the B cell epitope on a synthetic peptide containing the crossreactive B cell epitope.

a single synthetic peptide can contain T cell and B cells recognition sites for the pre-S(2), region of HBs Ag and that the synthetic peptide can prime T cell responses which provide help for B cell responses to the native pre-S2 region.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a synthetic vaccine for hepatitis B.
the molecular basis for T cell recognition of an epitope in a synthetic peptide corresponding to a region in the native HBsAg/p34/p33 protein.
the molecular definition of the immune response to a synthetic peptide, p 120-145, which contains both T cell and B-cell recognition sites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the synthetic peptide, p 120-145, is a useful immunogen, and the data presented here suggest that the immunogenicity may be due to a combination of T cell and B-cell recognition sites.

the T and B cell recognition of the pre-S(2), synthetic p120-145 is not a simple case of a T cell recognition site being identical to a B cell recognition site, and that the immunogenicity and H-2 restriction patterns for T and B cell sites are different.

T cell and antibody recognition of the synthetic pre-S(2), p120-145 peptide are both regulated by H- 2-linked genes, that the pattern of restriction differs between the T cell and antibody response, that there are dominant and nonoverlapping recognition sites, that T cell recognition is focused on the NH2 terminus and antibody recognition on the COOH terminus, that the fine specificity of T and B cell recognition is determined by a single, H-2-relevant amino acid residue
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a synthetic peptide can be used to define T cell and B-cell recognition sites on a complex antigen and to study their interaction in a functional immune response.
the synthetic peptide p145-120 is an effective T cell immunogen, but is only minimally recognized by antibody.
the synthetic peptide p145-120 contains two nonoverlapping determinants, one recognized by T cells and the other recognized by B cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immune response is a very complex process and that it is not always easy to predict the outcome of an immune response.
the immune response of the synthetic peptide pS(2) is regulated by H2-linked genes.
T and B cell sites can be separated on a single antigenic determinant, and that the synthetic B cell determinant can prime for antibody production to native HBsAg/p32 or p33 particles.
